note: Every string the menu can draw. The target machine is a Chromebook, whose top row is browser keys, so no F-key appears anywhere in this file or in the engine. The game is fully playable with a mouse and no keyboard at all: the panel button opens this menu, and every route through it is clickable. Ctrl+S and Ctrl+L are convenience only and are never the only way to reach anything.

sceneControls.note: ERRATA 71 B, from doc 34's coffin contract as errata 52 adopted it: in a room with no verb panel (Room 32), pointer intent reveals MENU -- the button label above -- and this, for a few seconds. SKIP SCENE lands on the same checkpoint watching does.

options.title: OPTIONS
options.musicNote: Doc 18 note 2's argument for the cycling toggle applies to a music bed for the same reason: it is continuous, it is not information, and a player who wants it off must be able to turn it off without leaving the game. Held with the other display preferences rather than in the save file -- a preference belongs to the machine, not to the game.
options.textSpeedNote: ERRATA 154 A. Doc 33 table 6: TEXT SPEED cycles SLOW / NORMAL / FAST / MANUAL; doc 30 table 2 names the same four settings Slow, Normal, Fast and Manual, in this menu's own case, and those are the labels. A click moves it one value on, wrapping after the last. Its value is a MACHINE SETTING (doc 33 section 7.3, textMode): stored apart from every save slot, so loading a slot, starting a new game or returning to the title never changes it. What each value does to a line is ui.json timing.textSpeeds. ERRATA 154 B. WINDOW SCALE IS GONE (doc 33 section 8.3: 'Remove the current inert Window scale row'). The frame fits the window as errata 54 rules (engine/main.ts); no row here changes it.

fullscreenNote: ERRATA 39 names the menu overlay and the verb panel, and this is the first. It sits above Quit to Title because it is the only root item that changes nothing about the game -- leaving it beside Resume would read as a state change and leaving it below Quit would put it after the exit.
